notes.britain-lf2: All 21 numbered Gruppen have locations in Collier. Independent station chronologies narrow some entries and contradict others, including the three JG 54 Gruppen listed in South Holland. Disputed locations are shown side by side. Where two places are reported for I./JG 51, only Saint-Inglevert is mapped.
notes.britain-lf2-hq: The eight headquarters have separate location entries. Some conflict with station chronologies, including JG 52 and JG 54. Their staff aircraft represent the headquarters element.
notes.britain-11g: The war-station and sector columns describe different things. No. 257 has two stations. No. 1 Squadron RAF and No. 1 Squadron RCAF have different bases. Activities carry their own dates.
notes.sicily-gruppen: The return lists four island-based Gruppen. The JG 51 station chronology dates a further Gruppe’s move from Sardinia to Trapani to 10 July, leaving the timing of the change unresolved. Ramacca can be identified within the Gerbini complex for II./JG 53.
notes.sicily-stab: The German return establishes where two headquarters were based. It does not place every Gruppe of either wing on the island.
notes.sicily-italian: The five identified gruppi are a lower bound. Chinisia and the Palermo detachment belong to one unit. The Catania locality does not resolve a runway.
notes.sicily-211: The five wing headings account for 23 assigned squadrons. HQ Malta’s 9 July disposition distinguishes aircraft at airfields from personnel in camp. The separate July refit evidence for 7 SAAF Wing cannot establish a 10 July sortie.
notes.sicily-xii: The five group names come from the 10 July command table. Gozo, Pantelleria and the Tunisian bases made support possible before the groups moved to Sicily. Dated activities are documented separately.
notes.citadel-gruppen: The 4 July assembly table puts four Gruppen around Orel and four on the southern axis. The northern locality covers several airfields. Holm’s III./JG 52 chronology names Ugrim where the initial assembly table offers two possibilities.
notes.bagration-air-armies: The five Soviet air armies are linked to front sectors across the offensive. The 6th Air Army supported the later left-wing operation. An air army normally operated from multiple fields.
